correctedState: The fork has no administrator-configurable shell-prefix env var: `grep -ain` for shell_prefix/shellprefix/process_wrapper/processwrapper across packages+apps returns zero hits. That much is real, and it applies to CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER (this page's actual subject) as well as CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX. But the finding's evidence and consequence are both wrong. The cited packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16320 is `executeDirectShellCommand`, the desktop composer bang-mode direct-shell RPC (error text :16400, tests in handlers/rpc/sessions.shell-command.test.ts) - not any of the three paths the doc sentence names. And shell commands do NOT all run unwrapped: Bash tool calls are wrapped before execution at packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:1477 via `applyBashSeatbeltSandbox`, whose `wrapBashCommandWithMacosSeatbelt` (bash-seatbelt.ts:123-137) emits `sandbox-exec -p <profile> /bin/bash -lc <shell-quoted command>` - a wrapper receiving the command as a single shell-quoted string, the same shape the doc describes for `$1`, with a host-owned fixed wrapper instead of an admin-supplied one. A parallel launcher mechanism covers the tool runtime (`resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher`: sandbox-exec/bwrap/firejail/unshare). The residual true gap is narrower: hooks (automations/hook-command.ts:717-726) and stdio MCP server startup (mcp/client.ts:392) are spawned with no wrapper hook, and the fork deliberately accepts only trusted absolute launchers, never an arbitrary admin string (pi-harness/isolation-remediation.ts:42).
